newsitem.title: UK: Littlewoods dampens reports of Lanica move.
newsitem.headline: Littlewoods dampens reports of Lanica move.

text.p: Privately-owned British retail and gambling group Littlewoods ruled out any use of Lanica Trust as a vehicle for listing of the group or a part of it.
"There is no truth in suggestions that it would be a listing vehicle for any part of Littlewoods," a company spokeswoman said.

The Times newspaper suggested on Tuesday that Lanica's shares have soared on rumours that Littlewoods might strike a deal with Freemans, the mail order part of retailer Sears Plc, to put together a package for a stock market listing with Lanica tipped as the vehicle.
Lanica's shares were trading at 19.75 stg by 1315 GMT, down 75 pence, compared with the 203 pence per share paid by entrepeneur Andrew Regan when he took control late last year.
One trader said there was constant buying interest in the stock from one or two "proper buyers and hundreds of scrappy buyers."
The Littlewoods spokeswoman said the company was discussing "the possibility of a very small fulfilment operation on the catalogue front" with Lanica.
Lanica changed its name from New Guernsey Securities after Regan took over.
Littlewoods is in talks with Sears on the possible purchase of Freemans, Britain's third largest mail order business.
Other companies reportedly interested in Freemans, which could carry a price tag of 350 to 400 million stg, include Manchester-based N Brown and German mail order group Otto Versand.
